question: PMMA dumanı için ISS dedektörü yanıtı

summary.text: In 2020 ground tests, the ISS scatter detector's response per unit smoke mass varied more across aerosol types than the other instruments (coefficient of variation 35%, versus 13% for a newer prototype).

technical_detail.text: Wang et al. (2020), p. 9: slopes of detector signal versus PM2.5 mass for reference and smoke aerosols; the authors attribute the ISS detector spread to its differing optics and plumbing. The ISS detector also saturated at higher concentrations.

Urban et al. (2026, NTRS 20260001992), Table 1 and alarm-threshold discussion: Saffire VI PMMA tests at 544 and 550 mbar with O2 mole fractions 0.30 and 0.29 reached 2 mg/m3 at 1037 s and 1603 s, when CO had risen 105 and 283 ppm (24-h SMAC 100 ppm). Flaming fires in an uncrewed Cygnus; the authors conclude a lower threshold or more detectors would be needed for that configuration.

Within the examined sources, the SAME/SAME-R atmosphere is inferred from the glovebox facility description (21% O2, 14.7 psi) because the experiment reports state only 'air'. Saffire IV-VI did measure flaming-fire smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor at up to 0.31 O2 mole fraction and 541 mbar, so flaming smoke at exploration-like atmospheres is partly covered; pyrolysis smoke and the ISS or Shuttle detectors are not.

Within the examined sources, an ionization detector's baseline changes at low pressure and must be characterised, and most reference aerosol instruments have limited use below Earth-ambient pressure. Saffire IV-VI flaming tests reached 541 mbar with a commercial ionization sensor.

condition.basis: inferred: SAME report says only 'air' inside the MSG and lists no gas-composition variation; the 2021 white paper (Table 1) gives the MSG atmosphere as 21% O2 at 14.7 psi
inferred: SAME-R report states no O2 or pressure; same MSG facility (21% O2, 14.7 psi per 2021 Table 1)
2021 white paper Table 1 lists GASP at 21% O2

detection_blindspots.statement: Within the examined sources, no spacecraft smoke-detector test with pre-fire (pyrolysis) smoke was run at elevated oxygen: SAME, SAME-R and the 2020 ground study used ordinary air at 21% O2, while the planned lunar habitat atmosphere is 34% O2 at 8.2 psi.
detection_blindspots.detail: The SAME/SAME-R atmosphere is inferred from the glovebox facility description (21% O2, 14.7 psi) because the experiment reports state only 'air'. Saffire IV-VI did measure flaming-fire smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor at up to 0.31 O2 mole fraction and 541 mbar, so flaming smoke at exploration-like atmospheres is partly covered; pyrolysis smoke and the ISS or Shuttle detectors are not.

detection_blindspots.topic: Smoke detection with pyrolysis smoke at reduced cabin pressure (<= 10.2 psi / 70.3 kPa)
detection_blindspots.rule: no detector-evaluating pyrolysis-smoke investigation profile with pressure min <= 70.3 kPa; any unknown pressure -> INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION
detection_blindspots.statement: Within the examined sources, no smoke-detector test with pyrolysis smoke was run at reduced pressure: the detector-evaluating pyrolysis tests ran at 14.7 psi, while Gateway HALO is nominally 10.2 psi and the planned lunar habitat 8.2 psi.
detection_blindspots.detail: An ionization detector's baseline changes at low pressure and must be characterised, and most reference aerosol instruments have limited use below Earth-ambient pressure. Saffire IV-VI flaming tests reached 541 mbar with a commercial ionization sensor.

detection_blindspots.topic: Heritage spacecraft smoke detectors exposed to flaming-fire smoke in microgravity
detection_blindspots.rule: no microgravity detector test with flaming-fire smoke for the ISS or Shuttle smoke detector

related_tests_other_detectors.detector: commercial ionization sensor + DustTrak DRX with assumed 2 mg/m3 alarm point

detection_blindspots.statement: Within the examined sources, the ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors were evaluated in microgravity only with pre-fire (pyrolysis) smoke, never with smoke from flaming fires; Saffire IV-VI measured flaming-fire smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor instead.
detection_blindspots.detail: SAME and SAME-R heated samples below ignition to emulate an overheat event. Saffire IV-VI fires were large flaming burns in an uncrewed Cygnus.

detection_blindspots.topic: ISS smoke-detector response to PMMA smoke
detection_blindspots.rule: material/detector pair not tested in microgravity with an alarm evaluation
detection_blindspots.statement: Within the examined sources, the ISS smoke detector was never tested with PMMA smoke in microgravity and no alarm decision was evaluated for PMMA smoke; its only exposure was a single 1 g ground test that measured signal against smoke mass.
detection_blindspots.detail: Saffire IV-VI burned PMMA in microgravity but measured smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor, not with the ISS detector. Model A (BASS-II PMMA flame spread) says nothing about smoke-detector response.

limitations: Results describe the cited experiments and documents only; they are not ISS fire-incident statistics or general detector failure rates.
Outputs are research-prioritisation aids, not a safety certification, alarm setting, or operational instruction.
Every gap statement is limited to the sources examined by this module ('within the examined sources'); absence in this collection does not mean NASA never studied the topic.
Model A (BASS-II flame spread) and Model B (Saffire-I ridge position) do not predict detector performance; no detection result is inferred from them.
Model C outputs are predictions of a derived 2.0 V threshold label (value_kind 'predicted'), never limitation evidence.
